transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-02-14
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Dr. Alan Kim (CTO - MediVentures), Sasha Martinez (Head of Infra), Rohit Patel (Security Architect)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Jordan Lee, account executive for Redwood. With me is Priya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Dr. Alan: Doing good, thanks. Busy week but excited to chat, we have a fairly strict timeline so hope we can cover requirements.
[00:12] Sasha: Hi all, Sasha here. I'll lead infra questions, we run most workloads in our data centers, little to no cloud for PHI.
[00:18] Rohit: Rohit, security. We'll focus on compliance controls and air-gapped update process.
[00:22] Priya: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: capture high-level goals, infra and security constraints, discuss deployment options (hosted / dedicated / private on-prem air-gapped), and next steps. Fair?
[00:30] Dr. Alan: Yep.

Summary / Goals
[00:38] Dr. Alan: We want to run Redwood inference on-prem for a triage/clinical assistant for doctors. Must be HIPAA-compliant, no PHI leaving our network. Ideally fully air-gapped so updates are manually approved.
[00:48] Jordan: Understood. Have you evaluated hosted or dedicated options first, or you're leaning straight to private because of the PHI rules?
[00:55] Sasha: We looked at Hosted but our legal said no. Dedicated could work but still goes over network boundaries. So private on-prem air-gapped is the lead option.
[01:05] Priya: Good. A few quick questions: what's your target latency and throughput, and do you have approved GPU types?
[01:12] Dr. Alan: Latency under 500ms p95 for single-user interactive queries ideally. Throughput is modest – maybe up to 50 concurrent sessions during peak. Hardware approved: A100 80GB nodes in our clusters. We have limited racks: only 4 GPUs per server, and no RDMA across racks right now.
[01:30] Priya: That helps. Our runtime supports A100s, and we can do batching to optimize cost vs latency. Noted about RDMA – that influences multi-node KV cache sharing.

Security / Compliance
[01:42] Rohit: Primary security asks: KMS/HSM integration for key material, full audit logs (who called what), SSO/SAML for user access, RBAC in the console, SOC2/ISO evidence, and an offline update path. Also need code signing for any package we install.
[01:58] Jordan: We have Redwood Private options that integrate with customer KMS and HSM, and the on-prem package can be deployed without external control plane connectivity. We support signed bundles for offline installs. Priya, want to add?
[02:08] Priya: Yeah, from a tech side we provide a signed tarball you import into your environment; the installer runs locally. For KMS, we can plug into an on-prem HSM using PKCS#11. Audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM or retained locally. Our Console can be run in a private control plane mode or fully offline with local UIs.
[02:25] Rohit: How do you manage updates? We need an approval gate and the ability to attest packages before installing.
[02:32] Priya: We support an air-gapped update process: Redwood generates a signed update bundle. Your security team verifies signatures, then you import and run the update in a maintenance window. We also provide a diff of model weights and runtime changes to speed review.
[02:44] Rohit: Good, and do you provide reproducible hashes for model artifacts?
[02:48] Priya: Yes, SHA256 hashes for every artifact and a manifest. We also support deterministic builds for runtime components.

Networking & Hardware Constraints
[03:00] Sasha: A couple infra constraints: limited cross-rack bandwidth, strict egress rules (no outbound to internet from model hosts), and our BMC/IPMI access is restricted. We also need to know cooling/power requirements for stacked A100s – we have limited power per rack.
[03:14] Priya: For power/cooling, we'll provide a hardware sizing guide. On the networking side, if you can't do RDMA multi-node, we can still run multi-node inference but with increased latency. Another option is to colocate KV-heavy workloads on the same rack or use model sharding with local cache.
[03:29] Jordan: Are you looking at quantization to reduce memory? That can let you fit more instances per GPU.
[03:33] Dr. Alan: Yes, we want to evaluate int8/4-bit quant with quality checks. Clinical accuracy cannot degrade beyond a specific delta.
[03:40] Priya: We have quantization profiles in Redwood Optimize and can run evals against your test set as part of the POC to measure regression. We'll recommend model variants and quant configs.

Operational / Rollout
[03:53] Dr. Alan: For the rollout, initial pilot on one rack with 4 A100-80GB nodes, then scale to two racks after validation. Maintenance windows are weekly on Sundays 02:00-05:00 local time.
[04:05] Jordan: Sounds reasonable. For pilot success criteria, can we align on: performance (p95 < 500ms), model output quality within X% of baseline, and zero unauthorized egress?
[04:16] Sasha: Yes. Also need runbook for incident response and for failback to manual process.
[04:22] Priya: We'll supply runbooks and automatable playbooks; also tracers you can integrate with your tracing system.

Objections & Tradeoffs
[04:34] Sasha: One concern: cost and ops overhead of private vs Redwood Dedicated. Can Redwood operate updates and monitoring on our behalf in an isolated model without direct internet access?
[04:45] Jordan: For fully air-gapped, we can offer an on-prem managed support add-on where we provide offline packages and remote support via a ticketing process, but we don't require inbound agents. For monitoring, logs stay local; we can accept periodic artifact uploads through a secure, customer-initiated channel if you want aggregated metrics.
[04:59] Rohit: If we later want to move to Dedicated or hosted, what is the migration path?
[05:03] Priya: The deployment abstraction keeps the API consistent. You can pin versions and move traffic between hosted/dedicated/private, but for PHI you'd have to re-validate compliance steps. We keep model version artifacts and the manifests so migration is straightforward from a technical perspective.

Shared Artifacts & References
[05:18] Jordan: We'll share: the air-gapped deployment checklist, the security whitepaper (SOC2/ISO/HIPAA notes), hardware sizing doc, and a sample signed update process. Also a template SOW for private deployment.
[05:28] Sasha: Please include expected timelines for installation and smoke test.
[05:31] Jordan: Yep.

Wrap-up / Next Steps
[05:36] Dr. Alan: Good call. Quick timeline question: how long to get pilot running once we approve hardware?
[05:42] Priya: Typical pilot install is 2-3 weeks including packaging and smoke tests if no unexpected infra blockers. If firmware and BMC access are constrained it can add time.
[05:51] Jordan: We'll target a technical deep dive next week to go through topology and sizing. I will send the docs by Tuesday.
[05:57] Dr. Alan: Sounds good.

[06:02] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials and schedule. Appreciate your time.
[06:06] Sasha: Thanks.
[06:08] Rohit: Thanks, bye.

Notes: Transcript has slight ASR errors (proper nouns sometimes off). References: 'air-gapped deployment checklist' (link sent after call), 'security_whitepaper.pdf' (link), 'hardware_sizing.xlsx' (link). End of transcript.
